summary:
[  edit  ]
The OAK Device  CHOP  serves as the main interface to an OAK camera. It also implements many of the features of the Timer  CHOP  such as timer counters, pulses, and custom Python callbacks.
Basic Usage
Before starting TouchDesigner, connect any OAK Devices to the computer via USB or Power over Ethernet (PoE). If you connect any devices while TouchDesigner is running, you should pulse the Refresh Device List parameter on the OAK Device  CHOP . Next, customize the Python createPipeline callback and pulse the start parameter to start the camera. It's ok if you save a project while a camera is running. The camera will know to automatically start when the project opens next time.
Resolution  and ISP Scale
The  depthai  python module has an enum for RGB resolution:  dai.ColorCameraProperties.SensorResolution . This enum currently includes THE_1080_P, THE_1200_P, THE_4_K, and many others. These options may not necessarily be compatible with your OAK hardware. The most commonly available RGB resolution is 1080p. You can save on bandwidth by selecting a lower resolution via the ISP scale. Selecting (2, 3) with THE_1080_P will result in a 1280x720 image.
Configs
The DepthaiTestSuite .toe  project includes several base components which help control settings of an OAK camera by sending messages via an OAK Device  CHOP . For example, the oakDeviceConfig base enables the user to set the XLinkChunkSize, logging level, and infrared laser settings of a device. The oakCameraControl base helps control RGB camera settings. The oakStereoDepthConfig base helps control stereo depth settings. It is possible to use these configs while the camera is running.
Optimizing Latency and  FPS
Luxonis has a tutorial on  low latency . In some cases such as streaming 4K video, you'll want to set  XLinkChunkSize  to zero. This can be done with the oakDeviceConfig.
When creating  depthai  pipelines, it's possible to set  FPS  targets for various nodes such as the  ColorCamera  node. In general, the  FPS  cannot be changed after the pipeline has been loaded on the camera. You should pick high  FPS  values, but keep in mind that if you push these numbers too high, you may see the effective  FPS  as shown by an Info  CHOP  begin to fall.
See Also:  OAK-D ,  OAK Select CHOP ,  OAK Select TOP

parameters.label: Sensor
parameters.name: sensor
parameters.description: Select the available OAK Device from the dropdown.

parameters.label: Refresh Sensor List
parameters.name: refreshpulse
parameters.description: Refresh the list of available Sensors.

parameters.label: Initialize
parameters.name: initialize
parameters.description: Initialize is the signal to get the OAK Device into a ready state: The   onInitialize  ()   callback is run and on succesfully concluding will run the   createPipeline  ()   callback. It indicates that its ready by turning the  ready  channel on.

parameters.label: Play
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: The built-in Play parameter can toggle whether or not TouchDesigner processes the new messages it receives from the camera. For example, suppose multiple OAK Select CHOPs or TOPs are connected to the same OAK Device  CHOP . By toggling play off, you will make all the OAK Select operators continue to receive whatever their most recently received message was, ignoring any new messages.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The path to the  DAT  containing callbacks for this OAK Device  CHOP .

parameters.label: The built
parameters.description: in page named Stream In helps with sending RGBA 8-bit images from TouchDesigner to an OAK camera. You can specify a  TOP , a stream name, and a sending frequency in Hertz. If the stream name is blank, nothing will be sent. When sending images to the OAK, TouchDesigner will convert the input image to BGR format. This is convenient because most of the neural networks which can be run on the OAK camera expect the input images to be BGR format. If you require the image to be something else, you should use the  ImageManip  node in your  depthai  pipeline to change the format.

parameters.label: Frequency (Hz)
parameters.name: stream0frequency
parameters.description: Specify the frequency at which a texture is being send to the OAK device.

parameters.label: TOP
parameters.name: stream0top
parameters.description: Specify the  TOP  operator that contains the texture to be send to the stream.

parameters.label: Initializing
parameters.name: outinit
parameters.description: Outputs channel  initializing  = 1 while the OAK Device is initalizing (i.e. while the callback   onInitialize  ()   returns non-zero).

parameters.label: Initialize Fail
parameters.name: outinitfail
parameters.description: Outputs channel  initialize_fail  = 1 if the OAK Device ran into an error while initializing or creating the pipeline.

parameters.label: Ready
parameters.name: outready
parameters.description: Outputs channel  ready  which is 1 after an Initialize and before a Start.

parameters.label: Running
parameters.name: outrunning
parameters.description: Outputs channel  running  which is 1 after a Start and before the Done.

parameters.label: Done
parameters.name: outdone
parameters.description: Outputs channel  done  = 1 when done or complete.

parameters.label: Running Time Count
parameters.name: outrunningcount
parameters.description: ⊞  - Outputs the "wall-clock" time since Start occurred, no matter if the device's  Play  parameter was turned off or not. Will stop counting when the  Done  state has been reached.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.
